definition: The 10-minute mean wind speed is the wind speed averaged over a ten-minute interval.
comment: Ten-minute averaging is the standard interval for wind measurements and turbine data, smoothing short gusts while preserving the variability relevant to resource assessment and power performance analysis. It is usually expressed in metres per second.

definition: Pressure of a fluid measured relative to a perfect vacuum.
comment: Atmospheric absolute pressure, typically expressed in pascals or hectopascals, is used together with temperature and humidity to compute air density. Air density in turn affects the power available in the wind and turbine output.

definition: The component of electrical power in an alternating-current system that performs useful work and is transferred as real energy.
comment: For wind turbines and other generators it represents the actual electrical output delivered to the grid and is the basis for power curves and energy yield calculations. It is usually expressed in kilowatts or megawatts.

definition: Quantity of water actually transferred from the land surface to the atmosphere by evaporation and plant transpiration under the prevailing water availability.
comment: It is a major loss term in the catchment water balance, usually expressed as a water depth per unit time. It reduces the share of precipitation that becomes runoff and therefore the water available for hydropower.

definition: Mass of air per unit volume.
comment: Air density, typically expressed in kilograms per cubic metre, depends on pressure, temperature and humidity. Wind power density and turbine power output are directly proportional to it, so it is used to correct power curves for site conditions.

definition: The amount of water vapour present in the air.
comment: Humidity is usually reported as relative humidity in percent or as specific or absolute humidity. It affects air density, PV module behaviour and evaporation, and is a frequent input to solar radiation and energy models.

definition: The force per unit area exerted by the weight of the atmosphere at a given location.
comment: Air pressure is combined with temperature to compute air density, which directly scales the power available in the wind. It is usually expressed in hectopascals.

definition: Temperature of the ambient air near the location of interest.
comment: It is usually expressed in degrees Celsius or kelvin. It controls air density for wind power, affects photovoltaic module efficiency and drives evaporation and energy demand.

definition: Quantitative descriptors extracted from images of the whole sky dome captured by ground-based sky cameras.
comment: Such features characterise cloud cover, cloud motion and the appearance of the sun region in the image. They are used as predictors in short-term solar irradiance and photovoltaic power forecasting.

definition: The vertical height of a point above mean sea level.
comment: Altitude is usually given in metres. It influences air density, temperature, solar radiation and wind conditions, and is therefore a common input to resource estimation models.

definition: The temperature of the surrounding air at a site.
comment: It affects air density for wind power, the efficiency of photovoltaic modules and thermal plant performance, and is a common predictor in energy and climate models. It is usually expressed in degrees Celsius.

definition: Temperature of the surrounding air at the place where a system or measurement is located.
comment: It is usually given in degrees Celsius. In renewable-energy assessment it is used to compute air density for wind power and to estimate the operating temperature and efficiency of PV modules.

definition: Total amount of electrical energy generated by a power plant or system over one year.
comment: Annual energy generation, typically expressed in megawatt-hours or terawatt-hours per year, is a key output of resource assessments. It underpins capacity factor, revenue and levelised cost calculations.

definition: The total energy produced by a generating unit or plant over one year.
comment: Usually expressed in megawatt-hours or gigawatt-hours per year, it is a central performance indicator for comparing sites and technologies. It underlies capacity factor and levelised cost calculations.

definition: The total electrical energy generated by a power plant or generator over one year.
comment: It is the central yield metric in renewable-energy project assessment, used to compute capacity factor, levelized cost of energy and revenues. It is typically expressed in kilowatt-hours, megawatt-hours or gigawatt-hours per year.

definition: Total volume or depth of water leaving a catchment as surface and subsurface flow over one year.
comment: Annual water yield reflects the balance between precipitation and evapotranspiration in a catchment. It indicates the water available for hydropower generation, water supply and other uses.

definition: The total electrical energy produced by a wind turbine or wind farm over one year.
comment: It is typically obtained by combining the wind speed distribution at hub height with the turbine power curve and is expressed in megawatt-hours or gigawatt-hours per year. It is the key quantity for assessing the economic viability of a wind project.

definition: The total electrical energy generated by a wind turbine over one year.
comment: It is obtained by combining the site wind speed distribution with the turbine power curve and is used to compare turbines and sites and to assess project economics. It is usually expressed in megawatt-hours per year.

definition: Vertical extent of a water-bearing geological formation between its upper and lower boundaries.
comment: It is usually expressed in metres. It controls how much groundwater an aquifer can store and transmit, which matters for groundwater resource assessment and water supply for energy projects.

definition: Amount of energy per unit area that a renewable resource makes available over a given period.
comment: For wind it is usually derived from the wind-speed distribution and air density, typically expressed in kilowatt-hours per square metre. It quantifies the theoretical resource before conversion losses and is used to compare and rank sites.

definition: The vertical difference in water level or elevation that can be exploited to drive a hydraulic turbine.
comment: Head, usually in metres, together with flow rate determines the power a hydropower scheme can produce. It is often estimated from topographic data during site screening.

definition: The kinetic power of the wind flowing through a unit area perpendicular to the flow at a site.
comment: It summarises the wind resource independently of any particular turbine and depends on air density and the cube of wind speed. It is usually expressed in watts per square metre.

definition: Mean value of the air temperature over a specified averaging period.
comment: It is usually expressed in degrees Celsius. Averaged temperature summarises the thermal climate of a site and is used as an input to models of energy demand, evapotranspiration and PV performance.

definition: Mean electrical power or energy delivered by a turbine over a specified period.
comment: It is obtained by combining the turbine power curve with the distribution of the driving resource at the site. It is used to estimate annual energy production and capacity factor of a turbine.

definition: The mean electrical power delivered by a wind turbine over a given period.
comment: It is commonly computed by integrating the turbine power curve over the wind speed probability distribution and is expressed in kilowatts or megawatts. Divided by rated power, it gives the capacity factor.

definition: Pressure exerted by the weight of the atmosphere at a given location, as measured by a barometer.
comment: It is usually expressed in hectopascals or millibars. Together with temperature it is used to compute air density, which directly scales the power available in the wind.

definition: The probability density function that best represents an empirical data distribution according to a chosen goodness-of-fit criterion.
comment: Selecting the best-fitting distribution, for example among Weibull, Rayleigh or gamma models for wind speed, improves the accuracy of derived energy estimates. Goodness-of-fit statistics are used to rank candidate distributions.

definition: Frequency with which wind speeds at a site fall to zero or below a calm threshold.
comment: It is usually expressed as a percentage or fraction of observations. A high calm frequency lowers the usable wind resource and is often treated separately when fitting wind-speed distributions.

definition: Ratio of the actual energy produced by a generating unit over a period to the energy it would produce operating continuously at rated power over the same period.
comment: Capacity factor, expressed as a fraction or percentage, summarises how effectively installed capacity is used given resource variability and availability. It is a standard metric for comparing sites, technologies and project economics.

definition: Volume of water per unit time leaving a catchment at its outlet.
comment: Catchment discharge, typically expressed in cubic metres per second, integrates rainfall, runoff and storage processes in a basin. It is the main driver of run-of-river and reservoir hydropower generation and is used to calibrate hydrological models.

definition: The operating temperature of a photovoltaic cell.
comment: Cell temperature, usually in degrees Celsius, rises above ambient temperature under irradiance and reduces PV conversion efficiency. It is estimated with thermal models from irradiance, air temperature and wind speed.

definition: A tradable carbon credit representing one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent of emissions reduction verified under a recognised crediting mechanism.
comment: Certified emission reductions provide an additional revenue stream for renewable-energy projects and are used to evaluate carbon-finance potential. They are counted in credits, each corresponding to one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent.

definition: Ratio of the observed solar irradiance at the surface to the irradiance expected under cloudless sky conditions at the same time and location.
comment: The clear-sky index removes the deterministic effects of sun position and atmosphere so that cloud-induced variability can be isolated. It is widely used in solar forecasting and in characterising sky conditions.

definition: The ratio of global solar radiation received at the surface to the extraterrestrial solar radiation on a horizontal plane.
comment: This dimensionless index describes atmospheric transparency and cloudiness. It is widely used to estimate diffuse and direct radiation components and to classify sky conditions.

definition: Degree to which a local community is aware of, consulted on, participates in or owns renewable-energy projects.
comment: Community engagement influences social acceptance, local benefit sharing and the likelihood that projects are approved and sustained. It is often treated as a qualitative criterion in renewable-energy planning and policy studies.

definition: The gross head of a hydropower site after adjustment for known measurement errors.
comment: Gross head is the total elevation difference between intake and outlet, usually in metres. Correcting it for positioning or elevation errors yields more reliable estimates of hydropower potential.

definition: An artificial inflow or outflow added to a hydraulic or hydrological model to bring simulated states closer to observations.
comment: It is a data-assimilation device that compensates for model and input errors, improving the reliability of simulated discharge and water levels used for hydropower operation. It is usually expressed in cubic metres per second.

definition: Diffuse solar radiation received on a horizontal surface totalled over one day.
comment: Diffuse radiation is the part of solar radiation scattered by the atmosphere and clouds before reaching the surface, typically expressed in watt-hours or megajoules per square metre per day. Its share of global radiation affects the yield of tilted and concentrating solar systems.

definition: The direct beam component of solar radiation totalled over one day.
comment: Direct radiation arrives from the solar disc without scattering and is usually expressed in watt-hours or megajoules per square metre per day. It is particularly relevant for concentrating solar and tracking systems.

definition: The total direct and diffuse solar radiation received on a horizontal surface accumulated over one day.
comment: It is the most common measure of the solar resource at a site and is used to size photovoltaic and solar thermal systems and to calibrate radiation models. It is usually expressed in megajoules or kilowatt-hours per square metre per day.

definition: The river discharge that is equalled or exceeded for a specified percentage of time.
comment: Derived from the flow-duration curve, it indicates the flow reliably available for generation and is used to size run-of-river hydropower plants. It is usually expressed in cubic metres per second.

definition: River discharge selected as the reference flow for sizing a hydraulic structure or hydropower plant.
comment: It is usually expressed in cubic metres per second and is often taken from the flow duration curve at a chosen exceedance probability. It sets turbine capacity and therefore the installed power and energy yield of a scheme.

definition: Ratio of diffuse solar radiation to global solar radiation on a horizontal surface.
comment: The diffuse fraction is dimensionless and indicates how much of the incoming radiation has been scattered by the atmosphere. It is used to separate global radiation into beam and diffuse components for modelling irradiance on tilted surfaces.

definition: The instantaneous solar power per unit area reaching a surface after scattering by the atmosphere and clouds.
comment: Diffuse irradiance, usually in watts per square metre, complements direct irradiance to form global irradiance. It matters for PV yield on tilted surfaces and under cloudy conditions.

definition: The part of solar radiation reaching a surface after being scattered by the atmosphere, clouds and particles.
comment: Separating diffuse from direct radiation is needed to estimate irradiance on tilted surfaces and to assess the suitability of concentrating versus flat-plate solar technologies. It is expressed in watts per square metre for irradiance or in energy per square metre for irradiation.

definition: Solar irradiance arriving at a surface directly from the solar disc without being scattered by the atmosphere.
comment: It is usually expressed in watts per square metre. It is the main input for concentrating solar systems and, with diffuse irradiance, determines the radiation received by tilted PV modules.

definition: Solar irradiance received directly from the solar disc on a surface held perpendicular to the sun rays.
comment: Direct normal irradiance, typically expressed in watts per square metre or as an annual total in kilowatt-hours per square metre, excludes scattered light. It is the key resource variable for concentrating solar power and tracking photovoltaic systems.

definition: The direct beam solar energy received per unit area on a surface held perpendicular to the sun's rays over a given period.
comment: It is the primary resource indicator for concentrating solar power and tracking PV systems. It is commonly reported in kilowatt-hours per square metre over a day or a year.

definition: The part of solar radiation that reaches a surface directly from the solar disc without being scattered.
comment: Direct radiation determines the performance of concentrating solar technologies and contributes to irradiance on tilted photovoltaic modules. It is expressed in watts per square metre for irradiance or in energy per square metre for irradiation.

definition: Difference between the discharge at a given time and a reference mean discharge for the same location and period.
comment: It is expressed in cubic metres per second. Such anomalies highlight wet and dry periods and help analyse hydrological variability affecting hydropower generation.

definition: The total length of stream channels per unit area of a drainage basin.
comment: Drainage density, usually in kilometres per square kilometre, reflects landscape dissection and runoff behaviour. It is used as a criterion in hydropower site suitability analyses.

definition: The hydraulic head actually available to a hydropower turbine after hydraulic losses are subtracted from the gross head.
comment: Together with discharge and efficiency it determines the power output of a hydropower plant. It is usually expressed in metres.

definition: Rate at which electrical energy is delivered by a generating unit or system.
comment: Electric power output, typically expressed in watts, kilowatts or megawatts, depends on the available resource and the conversion characteristics of the equipment. It is the basic quantity from which energy yield and performance indicators are derived.

definition: The intrinsic property of a material that quantifies how strongly it opposes electric current.
comment: In geophysical surveys, subsurface resistivity, in ohm metres, helps identify lithology and groundwater-bearing layers. Such information supports site investigations for water and energy infrastructure.

definition: Amount of electrical energy or power required by consumers over a given period.
comment: Electricity demand, typically expressed in kilowatt-hours per day or similar units, determines the size of generation and storage needed in a power system. Matching it with variable renewable supply is central to system design and dispatch.

definition: Electricity grid capacity is the maximum amount of power that transmission and distribution networks can carry or accept.
comment: Limited grid capacity can constrain the connection of new renewable plants and lead to curtailment, making it a key criterion in siting and planning studies. It is usually expressed in megawatts.

definition: Amount of energy required by consumers or a system over a given period.
comment: It may refer to electricity or other energy forms and is expressed in energy units per time. Demand profiles are matched against renewable supply to size plants, storage and grid connections.

definition: Amount of energy per unit area or volume carried by or available from a resource over a given period.
comment: In renewable-energy assessment it typically refers to the energy flux of wind or water through a unit area, expressed for example in kilowatt-hours per square metre. It is used to quantify and compare the size of resources between sites.

definition: An index that expresses how effectively energy input is converted into useful output for a system or process.
comment: Efficiency indices are often given as percentages and allow performance to be tracked over time or compared between systems. Low values indicate losses that may be reduced by technical or operational improvements.

definition: Measure of the effects of a hydropower project on the natural environment.
comment: It can be expressed through indicators such as installed capacity per flooded area or affected ecosystems. It is used to compare projects and balance energy benefits against ecological and social costs.

definition: Numerical value expressing the relative importance assigned to a criterion in a multi-criteria evaluation.
comment: Criterion weights determine how individual criteria contribute to an overall score when ranking options. They are commonly derived from expert judgement or pairwise comparison methods in renewable-energy planning.

definition: The combined transfer of water to the atmosphere by evaporation from surfaces and transpiration from plants.
comment: It is a major loss term in the water balance, controlling how much precipitation becomes runoff available for hydropower and reservoir storage. It is usually expressed in millimetres of water over a period.

definition: The solar radiation received on a horizontal surface at the top of the atmosphere.
comment: It is computed from astronomical relations depending on latitude, day of year and solar geometry. It serves as the reference for clearness index and many empirical models of surface solar radiation.

definition: The solar radiation received on a horizontal surface at the top of the atmosphere.
comment: It depends only on latitude, date and time and serves as the reference for computing the clearness index and for empirical models estimating surface solar radiation. It is usually expressed in megajoules or watt-hours per square metre per day.

definition: Wind speed of an exceptionally high value expected to be reached or exceeded with a given return period.
comment: It is usually expressed in metres per second. It is used to select turbine classes and design structures to withstand rare but severe wind events.

definition: The amount of energy a generating system can deliver with a specified high reliability over a given period.
comment: Firm energy indicates guaranteed supply, especially for hydropower plants subject to variable inflows. It is usually expressed in gigawatt-hours per year and is important for planning and contracting.

definition: The minimum river discharge that is reliably available at a high level of dependability over time.
comment: It sets the guaranteed or firm power that a hydropower plant can deliver and is a key parameter in plant design and planning. It is usually expressed in cubic metres per second.

definition: Power output that a plant can guarantee to supply continuously with a high level of reliability.
comment: It is usually expressed in megawatts or kilowatts and, for hydropower, is tied to a dependable flow. It indicates the share of capacity that can be counted on to meet demand.

definition: Volume of fluid, typically water, passing a given cross-section per unit time.
comment: Flow, typically expressed in cubic metres per second, is a basic quantity in hydraulics and hydrology. Together with available head it determines the power that can be extracted by hydropower installations.

definition: The direction in which surface water flows from a terrain cell to its steepest downslope neighbour.
comment: Flow direction rasters are derived from digital elevation models. They are the basis for computing flow accumulation, stream networks and catchment boundaries in hydropower site studies.

definition: The probability that river discharge equals or exceeds a given value.
comment: It forms the horizontal axis of the flow-duration curve and is used to select design flows and estimate the reliability of hydropower generation. It is usually expressed as a percentage of time.

definition: Velocity scale defined from the turbulent shear stress at the surface and the air density.
comment: Friction velocity, typically expressed in metres per second, characterises the intensity of mechanical turbulence near the ground. It is a key parameter in similarity theory for describing the vertical wind profile in the surface layer.

definition: The quantity of gasoil that would be needed to produce the same amount of energy as another source.
comment: Fuel equivalence expresses renewable energy output in terms of displaced fossil fuel, usually in tonnes. It helps communicate fuel savings and associated economic benefits.

definition: The quantity of gasoline that would contain or produce the same amount of energy as a given energy quantity.
comment: Expressing renewable output as a fossil-fuel equivalent conveys the fuel savings and substitution value of renewable generation. It is usually expressed in tonnes or litres of gasoline.

definition: Maximum electrical power that a generating unit, plant or set of plants can deliver.
comment: It is usually expressed in megawatts. It describes the size of the generation fleet and, together with capacity factor, determines potential energy output.

definition: Scheduled amount of electrical generation assigned to a power system or plant for each period of an operating horizon.
comment: Generation plans are prepared from load and resource forecasts to coordinate dispatch of units. In systems with variable renewables they help balance forecast output against demand.

definition: The difference between the actual power output of a generating system and its scheduled generation plan.
comment: Deviations, usually in megawatts, reflect forecast errors and the variability of renewable sources. Reducing them is important for grid operation and can avoid imbalance penalties.

definition: The total direct and diffuse solar radiant power received per unit area on a horizontal surface.
comment: It is the primary measured quantity for solar resource assessment and the starting point for estimating irradiance on tilted photovoltaic modules. It is usually expressed in watts per square metre.

definition: Total solar radiation energy received on a horizontal surface over a given period, combining direct and diffuse components.
comment: It is usually expressed in kilowatt-hours per square metre per day or per year. It is the primary indicator of solar resource quality for PV siting and yield estimation.

definition: Total solar irradiance received on a surface, comprising direct and diffuse components.
comment: Global irradiance, typically expressed in watts per square metre and usually referring to a horizontal surface, is the primary solar resource variable. It drives photovoltaic output and is the basis for most solar resource assessments.

definition: The total solar radiation, direct and diffuse, received on a horizontal surface over a given period.
comment: It is the primary solar resource variable and is commonly expressed in megajoules or kilowatt-hours per square metre per day. It is the main input for sizing and estimating the yield of solar energy systems.

definition: The total solar radiant power received per unit area on an inclined surface, including direct, diffuse and ground-reflected components.
comment: It represents the irradiance actually incident on tilted photovoltaic modules and is therefore the direct input for photovoltaic yield estimation. It is usually expressed in watts per square metre.

definition: The total vertical elevation difference between the water intake level and the turbine outlet or tailwater level of a hydropower scheme.
comment: It defines the maximum hydraulic energy available per unit of water before losses and, together with discharge, determines hydropower potential. It is usually expressed in metres.

definition: Relative capacity of an area to host, transmit and store exploitable groundwater.
comment: It is often expressed as a categorical class derived from geological, terrain and land-cover factors. It supports water resource planning and the siting of water supply for energy and other uses.

definition: Volume of water held in the saturated zone beneath the land surface, often expressed as an equivalent water depth.
comment: Groundwater storage, typically expressed in millimetres of water equivalent, is a component of terrestrial water storage. It sustains baseflow to rivers and therefore affects the long-term reliability of water resources, including for hydropower.

definition: The ratio of the elevation difference available for hydropower to the horizontal distance over which it is obtained.
comment: High ratios indicate steep sites where substantial head can be developed with short waterways, making it a useful screening criterion for small hydropower and pumped-storage sites. It is dimensionless.

definition: Total solar radiation, direct plus diffuse, received on a horizontal surface.
comment: It is expressed as irradiance in watts per square metre or as irradiation over a period. It is the basic measured quantity used to characterise the solar resource and estimate PV yield.

definition: Magnitude of the horizontal component of the wind velocity vector.
comment: Horizontal wind speed, typically expressed in metres per second, is the quantity measured by most anemometers. It is the basic input for wind resource assessment, wind power density and turbine energy yield calculations.

definition: Wind speed averaged over one hour.
comment: Hourly means, usually in metres per second, are a common resolution for wind measurements and reanalysis data. They are used to fit wind speed distributions and estimate energy production.

definition: The amount of water vapour present in the air.
comment: Humidity influences air density, cloud formation and atmospheric transmittance, and is used as a predictor in solar radiation, wind and hydrological models. It is expressed as relative humidity in percent or as specific humidity in kilograms per kilogram.

definition: Vertical height difference of water between two points that drives flow and determines its potential energy.
comment: It is usually expressed in metres. In hydropower, the available head combined with discharge determines the power that can be generated.

definition: Kinetic power carried by flowing water per unit of cross-sectional flow area.
comment: Hydro-kinetic power density, typically expressed in watts per square metre, is proportional to water density and the cube of flow velocity. It is used to assess the resource for in-stream turbines that do not require a dam or head.

definition: The kinetic energy of flowing water that is theoretically available for conversion into electricity without a dam.
comment: It depends on water velocity and cross-sectional area and is usually expressed as power in watts or kilowatts. It is used to assess sites for in-stream river and tidal turbines.

definition: The degree to which the flow regime of a river departs from its natural or pre-impact variability.
comment: It is used to assess the environmental impact of dams and hydropower operation on downstream ecosystems, often through indicators of hydrologic alteration. It is typically expressed as a dimensionless index or percentage.

definition: Maximum electrical power that a hydropower plant or set of hydropower plants can produce.
comment: It is usually expressed in megawatts. It describes the size of existing or planned hydropower development and is used in energy planning and potential assessments.

definition: Ratio of the energy actually generated by a hydropower plant over a period to the energy it would generate at full installed capacity over the same period.
comment: The hydropower capacity factor, expressed as a fraction or percentage, reflects water availability, reservoir operation and plant availability. It is used to compare plant performance and to evaluate the effects of hydrological variability.

definition: The electrical energy produced by a hydropower plant over a given period.
comment: It is usually expressed in megawatt-hours or gigawatt-hours and depends on discharge, head and plant efficiency. It is the main output variable in hydropower operation and forecasting studies.

definition: The electrical energy produced by hydroelectric plants over a period.
comment: It is the main output of hydropower systems and the target of forecasting, operation and planning studies linking hydrology to electricity supply. It is usually expressed in megawatt-hours or gigawatt-hours.

definition: Proportion of total electricity generation supplied by hydropower.
comment: It is usually expressed as a percentage. It reflects the dependence of an electricity system on hydropower and its exposure to hydrological variability.

definition: Composite index expressing the environmental impact of hydropower as a combination of population, affluence and technology factors.
comment: The IPAT framework represents environmental impact as the product of population, affluence and technology. Applied to hydropower, such an index is used to compare environmental pressure across regions or periods.

definition: The amount of hydropower that could be developed from the water resources of a given area.
comment: It may be expressed as power capacity or annual energy and may refer to theoretical, technical or economic potential. It guides national and regional planning of hydropower development.

definition: The electrical energy or power produced by a hydroelectric plant.
comment: It reflects the combined effect of discharge, head and plant efficiency and is used to evaluate plant performance and contribution to electricity supply. It is expressed in energy units such as megawatt-hours or in power units such as kilowatts.

definition: Distance between a hydropower site and a reference feature such as a road, settlement or grid connection.
comment: It is usually expressed in metres or kilometres. Distance affects construction, access and connection costs and is therefore used in site suitability analysis.

definition: The total rated electrical power of hydroelectric generating units in operation.
comment: It indicates the scale of hydropower development in a plant, region or country and is used with generation data to compute capacity factors. It is usually expressed in megawatts.

definition: Reciprocal of the Obukhov length, a scaling parameter of the atmospheric surface layer that expresses the relative importance of buoyancy and shear in generating turbulence.
comment: It is expressed in inverse metres, with its sign indicating stable or unstable stratification. It is used to classify atmospheric stability and correct wind profiles for vertical extrapolation to hub height.

definition: Amount of energy required to operate pumps that lift and deliver water for irrigation.
comment: Irrigation-pump energy demand, typically expressed in kilowatt-hours, depends on the water volume pumped and the total head. It is used to size renewable-powered pumping systems such as solar or wind water pumps.

definition: Dimensionless ratios of higher-order L-moments to the L-scale that describe the shape of a probability distribution.
comment: L-moment ratios such as L-skewness and L-kurtosis are robust to outliers. They are used to identify suitable distributions and regionalise variables such as wind speed or river flow.

definition: Classification of the land surface according to its physical cover and the human activities carried out on it.
comment: It is usually represented as categorical classes or areas per class. It influences runoff, groundwater recharge and surface roughness and constrains where energy infrastructure can be built.

definition: Angular distance of a location north or south of the equator.
comment: Latitude, typically expressed in degrees, determines solar geometry, day length and the extraterrestrial radiation a site receives. It is therefore a common input to solar radiation models.

definition: The theoretical hydropower potential of a river reach obtained by using its full discharge and the entire head along the reach.
comment: It represents an upper bound of the energy resource of a river before technical, economic and environmental constraints are applied. It is usually expressed in kilowatts or megawatts.

definition: Total length of linear geological or topographic features, such as faults and fractures, per unit area.
comment: It is usually expressed in kilometres per square kilometre. High lineament density indicates fractured rock that can enhance groundwater infiltration and storage.

definition: The ratio of the actual energy produced by a generating unit over a period to the energy it would produce at full rated power over the same period.
comment: Also called capacity factor, it is dimensionless or given as a percentage. It summarises how effectively a plant uses its installed capacity given resource variability.

definition: Water flowing into a reservoir from its immediate local catchment, excluding releases from upstream reservoirs.
comment: It is usually expressed in cubic metres per second. It is a key quantity for reservoir operation and for forecasting the water available for hydropower generation.

definition: Highest air temperature reached during a specified period.
comment: Maximum air temperature, typically expressed in degrees Celsius and commonly reported daily, is a standard meteorological observation. It is used in temperature-based solar radiation models and affects photovoltaic module temperature and efficiency.

definition: The wind speed that contributes the greatest amount of energy to the total wind energy at a site.
comment: It is derived from the parameters of the wind speed distribution, typically the Weibull distribution, and is expressed in metres per second. It is used to match turbine rated speed to the local wind regime.

definition: The length of time between sunrise and sunset during which direct sunshine could be received at a location in the absence of clouds.
comment: It depends on latitude and day of year and is used as the denominator of relative sunshine duration in empirical solar radiation models. It is usually expressed in hours.

definition: Operating point on the current-voltage characteristic of a photovoltaic device at which its electrical power output is highest.
comment: It depends on irradiance and cell temperature and is described by its power, current and voltage. Inverters use tracking algorithms to keep PV systems at this point and maximise energy yield.

definition: The average volume of water flowing through a river cross-section per unit time, computed over one year or averaged across years.
comment: Mean annual discharge, usually in cubic metres per second, characterises the water resource of a river. It is a fundamental input to hydropower potential estimation and model calibration.

definition: The average wind energy passing through a unit area perpendicular to the flow over a given period.
comment: It quantifies the wind energy resource accumulated over time and is used to compare sites and estimate potential turbine yields. It is usually expressed in kilowatt-hours per square metre.

definition: Average power carried by the wind per unit area perpendicular to the flow over a given period.
comment: It is usually expressed in watts per square metre and depends on air density and the cube of wind speed. It is a standard indicator for classifying and comparing wind resources at different sites.

definition: Average value of the scale parameter of the Weibull distribution fitted to wind-speed data.
comment: The Weibull scale parameter, expressed in the same units as wind speed such as metres per second, is closely related to the mean wind speed. Together with the shape parameter it is used to estimate wind power density and turbine energy yield.

definition: The average value of the shape parameter of the Weibull distribution over a set of samples, periods or sites.
comment: The Weibull shape parameter is dimensionless and describes the spread of wind speeds. Together with the scale parameter it determines the wind speed distribution used in energy yield estimates.

definition: The time-averaged kinetic power of the wind per unit area perpendicular to the flow.
comment: Because it accounts for the cube of wind speed and its distribution, it is a standard indicator for classifying wind resource quality at a site. It is usually expressed in watts per square metre.

variableName: mean wind power per unit area
definition: Average kinetic power of the wind passing through a unit area perpendicular to the flow.
comment: It is usually expressed in watts per square metre and is computed from air density and the wind-speed distribution. It quantifies the theoretical wind resource available before conversion losses.

definition: The north-south component of the horizontal wind vector.
comment: It is positive for wind blowing towards the north and is usually expressed in metres per second. Combined with the zonal component, it gives wind speed and direction in reanalysis and model data.

definition: The south-to-north component of the horizontal wind vector.
comment: Together with the zonal component it fully describes horizontal wind and is the form in which wind is provided by most reanalysis and weather models. It is usually expressed in metres per second.

definition: Component of the horizontal wind velocity directed along the north-south axis.
comment: It is usually expressed in metres per second, positive towards the north. Combined with the zonal component it gives wind speed and direction, and it is a standard output of reanalysis and weather models.

definition: Air temperature simulated or represented at the spatial resolution of a mesoscale atmospheric model.
comment: Mesoscale air temperature, typically expressed in degrees Celsius, describes atmospheric conditions over areas of a few to several hundred kilometres. It is used in wind and solar resource modelling, for example to derive air density and atmospheric stability.

definition: Atmospheric pressure at the Earth's surface as represented by a mesoscale atmospheric model.
comment: Surface pressure, usually in pascals or hectopascals, is used to compute air density and to characterise synoptic and mesoscale weather patterns. Both affect wind energy estimates.

definition: The direction from which the wind blows as represented at the mesoscale, over horizontal scales of a few to several hundred kilometres.
comment: Mesoscale wind direction captures regional flow patterns from models or reanalyses and is used in wind resource mapping, downscaling and wind farm layout analysis. It is usually expressed in degrees.

definition: Wind speed simulated or represented at the mesoscale, resolving atmospheric features of a few to several hundred kilometres.
comment: It is usually expressed in metres per second and is produced by mesoscale numerical models. It is used in wind atlases and as a large-scale input that is downscaled to estimate site-level wind conditions.

definition: Lowest air temperature reached during a specified period.
comment: Minimum air temperature, typically expressed in degrees Celsius and commonly reported daily, is a standard meteorological observation. Together with maximum temperature it is used in temperature-based models of solar radiation.

definition: Total electrical energy generated by hydropower plants over one month before deduction of auxiliary consumption and losses.
comment: Monthly gross hydropower production, typically expressed in gigawatt-hours, reflects seasonal water availability and plant operation. It is used to analyse hydrological variability and to forecast hydropower supply.

definition: The wind speed that occurs with the highest frequency in a wind speed distribution.
comment: It corresponds to the mode of the distribution and is typically derived from Weibull parameters, in metres per second. It helps characterise the local wind regime and inform turbine selection.

definition: Whether a municipality intends to develop renewable-energy projects.
comment: It reflects local institutional willingness to engage in renewable-energy deployment and is used in studies of the social and governance drivers of energy transitions.

definition: Quantity of natural gas that would provide the same amount of energy as a given amount of energy from another source.
comment: It is usually expressed in cubic metres. It is used to express renewable energy production in terms of displaced fossil fuel and the associated savings.

definition: Energy delivered by a generating system over a period after deduction of internal consumption and losses.
comment: Net energy output reflects the electricity actually available for use or sale. It is the basis for economic evaluation and for comparing the real performance of energy systems.

definition: The effective head available to a hydraulic turbine after subtracting hydraulic losses from the gross head.
comment: Net head, usually in metres, directly determines the power output of a hydropower plant for a given discharge. It varies with reservoir and tailwater levels.

definition: The hydraulic head available at a hydropower turbine after subtracting all hydraulic losses from the gross head.
comment: Net head, together with discharge and turbine efficiency, determines the power output and guides turbine selection. It is usually expressed in metres.

definition: Sum of all future cash inflows and outflows of a project discounted to their present value.
comment: It is expressed in currency units. A positive value indicates that a renewable-energy investment is profitable at the chosen discount rate, so it is widely used for project appraisal and optimisation.

definition: Radiance of artificial light emitted from the Earth surface at night as recorded by satellite sensors.
comment: Nighttime-light radiance is widely used as a proxy for human settlement, economic activity and electricity use. It helps estimate electricity access and demand in regions with limited statistics.

definition: The ratio of actual air density to a reference standard air density.
comment: It is used to correct wind turbine power curves and wind power density for site conditions that differ from standard atmosphere. It is dimensionless.

definition: Vertical distance from the sea surface to the seabed at a location.
comment: Ocean depth, typically expressed in metres, determines whether fixed-bottom or floating foundations are feasible for offshore wind turbines. It strongly influences installation cost and is a common criterion in offshore site selection.

definition: A composite score indicating how suitable a marine area is for offshore wind development.
comment: It is typically derived from geographic multi-criteria analysis combining resource, technical, environmental and socio-economic factors. It supports marine spatial planning and site selection.

definition: The probability that a wind turbine is in its operating range, with wind speed between the cut-in and cut-out speeds.
comment: It is derived from the wind speed distribution and the turbine characteristics and indicates the fraction of time a turbine can generate power at a site. It is expressed as a probability or percentage.

definition: Amount of energy delivered by a conversion system over a given period.
comment: It is usually expressed in kilowatt-hours, megawatt-hours or gigawatt-hours. It is the main performance result used to compare technologies and compute capacity factor and cost of energy.

definition: Maximum rate of water flow passing a point in a stream during a given event or period.
comment: Peak discharge, typically expressed in cubic metres per second, characterises flood magnitude. It is used in the design of spillways, intakes and other hydraulic structures of hydropower schemes.

definition: Maximum electrical power that a pumped hydro energy storage system can deliver in generating mode.
comment: It is usually expressed in megawatts. Together with storage energy capacity it determines how pumped hydro can balance variable renewable generation.

definition: Electrical power produced by a photovoltaic module, array or system.
comment: Photovoltaic power, typically expressed in watts or kilowatts, depends on irradiance, cell temperature and system characteristics. It is the primary output quantity in photovoltaic performance modelling and forecasting.

definition: The depth of the lowest part of the atmosphere that is directly influenced by the Earth's surface.
comment: Usually expressed in metres, it varies diurnally with surface heating and stability. It affects vertical mixing and the wind profile across the heights of turbine rotors.

definition: Power carried by or available from a resource per unit area.
comment: In renewable-energy assessment it usually refers to the power flux of wind or water through a unit area perpendicular to the flow, typically expressed in watts per square metre. It is used to classify and compare resource quality between sites.

definition: The composition of total electricity generation by source or technology.
comment: It is usually described as shares of thermal, hydro, nuclear and other renewable generation. It is used to characterise energy systems and track decarbonisation.

definition: Liquid or solid water falling from the atmosphere to the ground.
comment: Precipitation is the primary input to the catchment water balance and drives runoff and reservoir inflows that determine hydropower availability. It is usually expressed in millimetres over a period.

definition: Electric current produced by a photovoltaic cell, module or array.
comment: It is expressed in amperes and depends mainly on irradiance. Together with voltage it determines the electrical power output of a PV system.

definition: Electrical energy generated by a photovoltaic system over a given period.
comment: PV energy output, often expressed in kilowatt-hours or normalised per kilowatt-peak of installed capacity, summarises system yield. It is used to compare sites, designs and the economics of photovoltaic projects.

definition: The operating temperature of a photovoltaic module.
comment: Module temperature, usually in degrees Celsius, rises with irradiance and lowers conversion efficiency. It is modelled from irradiance, air temperature and wind speed to predict PV output.

definition: The electrical power produced by a photovoltaic module, array or system.
comment: It depends mainly on irradiance and module temperature and is the target of photovoltaic performance analysis and forecasting. It is usually expressed in watts or kilowatts.

definition: Electric potential difference across the terminals of a photovoltaic cell, module or array.
comment: It is expressed in volts and decreases with increasing cell temperature. Together with current it determines PV power output and is monitored for performance analysis.

definition: Amount of liquid precipitation reaching the ground over a given period.
comment: Rainfall, typically expressed in millimetres, is the main input of water to catchments. It drives runoff and streamflow and is therefore a key input for hydrological and hydropower modelling.

definition: The water discharge at which a hydraulic turbine produces its rated power output.
comment: Rated flow, usually in cubic metres per second, is a key design parameter of a hydropower plant. It is chosen in relation to the flow duration curve of the river.

definition: The component of electrical power in an alternating-current system that oscillates between source and load without performing net work.
comment: Generators such as wind turbines produce or absorb reactive power to support voltage control and meet grid connection requirements. It is usually expressed in kilovolt-ampere reactive.

definition: Amount of energy that can actually be extracted from a resource by a given conversion system.
comment: It is usually expressed in kilowatt-hours. For wind, it is obtained by combining the wind-speed distribution with a turbine power curve, giving a realistic yield estimate rather than the theoretical resource.

definition: Portion of wind power density that can theoretically be extracted by a wind turbine given the limit on aerodynamic conversion efficiency.
comment: It is usually computed by applying the Betz limit, a maximum fraction of about 59 percent, to the total wind power density, typically expressed in watts per square metre. It indicates the upper bound of usable wind power at a site.

definition: The solar radiant power per unit area reaching a surface after reflection from the ground or surrounding surfaces.
comment: It contributes to the total irradiance on tilted and bifacial photovoltaic modules and depends on surface albedo. It is usually expressed in watts per square metre.

definition: Elevation of a point expressed relative to a local reference surface rather than to sea level.
comment: It is usually expressed in metres. It indicates whether a location is exposed on a ridge or sheltered in a depression, which affects local wind speed and drainage.

definition: Ratio of the actual water vapour content of air to the maximum it can hold at the same temperature, expressed as a percentage.
comment: Relative humidity affects air density, cloud formation and atmospheric transmittance. It is used as a predictor in solar radiation models and in correcting wind power estimates.

definition: The ratio of the actual duration of bright sunshine to the maximum possible sunshine duration over a given period.
comment: This dimensionless ratio is a widely available proxy for cloudiness. It is the main predictor in Angstrom-type models for estimating global solar radiation.

definition: The ratio of measured sunshine duration to the maximum possible sunshine duration.
comment: It is the main predictor in Angstrom-type empirical models used to estimate global solar radiation where radiation measurements are lacking. It is dimensionless.

definition: Proportion of electricity generation or consumption supplied by renewable energy sources.
comment: It is usually expressed as a percentage. It is a central indicator for tracking energy transition progress and policy targets.

definition: Extent to which renewable-energy technologies are taken up and deployed by users, communities or countries.
comment: Adoption reflects the combined influence of technical, economic, social and policy factors. It is a central outcome studied in energy-transition and policy analyses.

definition: The rated significance of a given obstacle to the deployment of renewable-energy projects.
comment: Such ratings, typically elicited from stakeholders on ordinal scales, help prioritise policy and market interventions to accelerate renewable-energy uptake.

definition: Overall effect of a renewable-energy strategy on the conditions or barriers it is intended to address.
comment: Strategy impact is often estimated by aggregating weighted effects across several barriers or criteria. It is used to prioritise policy options for promoting renewable energy.

definition: The relative ranking of a strategy for promoting renewable energy or mitigating barriers to its adoption.
comment: Priorities are typically derived from multi-criteria decision methods based on expert assessments. They guide the sequencing of policy and investment actions.

definition: The height of the water surface in a reservoir above a reference datum.
comment: It determines the available head and storage of a hydropower reservoir and is a key state variable in reservoir operation and generation forecasting. It is usually expressed in metres.

definition: Quantity of water lost to the atmosphere by evaporation from the free surface of a reservoir.
comment: It is usually expressed as a water depth or volume per period. It reduces stored water available for hydropower and must be included in reservoir water balances.

definition: Volume of water entering a reservoir per unit time or over a given period.
comment: Reservoir inflow, expressed as a flow rate such as cubic metres per second or as a volume per period, determines the water available for storage and release. It is a primary forecast target for hydropower scheduling and water management.

definition: The volume or rate of water discharged from a reservoir over a given period.
comment: Releases are controlled to meet power generation, irrigation, flood control and downstream flow requirements. They are a key decision variable in reservoir operation optimisation.

definition: The volume of water held in a reservoir at a given time.
comment: Storage determines how much water can be released for generation and is central to reservoir operation planning and hydropower forecasting. It is usually expressed in cubic metres or million cubic metres.

definition: Quantity of water stored in a reservoir at a given time or at a specified level.
comment: It is usually expressed in cubic metres or millions of cubic metres. Storage volume determines the energy that can be generated and the ability of a hydropower plant to regulate flows.

definition: Height of the water surface in a reservoir relative to a reference datum.
comment: Reservoir water elevation, typically expressed in metres, determines stored volume and the available head for hydropower generation. It is monitored and forecast to guide reservoir operation.

definition: The elevation of the water surface in a reservoir relative to a reference datum.
comment: Usually expressed in metres, it determines storage volume and the head available for power generation. It is a central state variable in reservoir operation.

definition: The portion of river discharge that is not diverted for use and remains in the river downstream of an intake.
comment: It is required to sustain downstream ecosystems and water uses and is deducted from available discharge when estimating hydropower potential. It is usually expressed in cubic metres per second.

definition: Volume of water flowing through a river cross-section per unit time.
comment: River discharge rate, typically expressed in cubic metres per second, can be computed as mean flow velocity multiplied by cross-sectional area. It is a fundamental input for estimating hydropower potential.

definition: The volume of water passing through a river cross-section per unit time.
comment: River flow, or discharge, is usually given in cubic metres per second. It is the primary resource variable for hydropower and a key boundary condition in hydraulic modelling.

definition: The volume of water passing through a river cross-section per unit time.
comment: It is the fundamental hydrological quantity for hydropower assessment, determining together with head the power that can be generated. It is usually expressed in cubic metres per second.

definition: Height above the surface at which the wind speed extrapolated from the logarithmic wind profile becomes zero.
comment: Roughness length, typically expressed in metres, depends on the surface cover and obstacles. It is used to describe the vertical wind profile and to extrapolate wind speed to turbine hub height.

definition: The extent to which run-of-river hydropower development meets environmental, social and economic sustainability requirements.
comment: Run-of-river schemes divert river flow with little or no storage. Their sustainability depends on factors such as ecological flows, community acceptance and economic viability.

definition: The portion of precipitation that flows over or through the land surface into streams and rivers.
comment: Runoff determines the water available for river flow and reservoir inflow and is therefore central to estimating hydropower resources. It is usually expressed as a depth of water, such as millimetres per year, or as a flow rate.

definition: Vertical distance from the sea surface to the seabed at a given location.
comment: It is usually expressed in metres and derived from bathymetric data. Water depth constrains offshore wind siting and determines the choice and cost of turbine foundations.

definition: Shortwave solar radiation reaching a surface after being scattered by the atmosphere, clouds or aerosols.
comment: Diffuse incident shortwave radiation, typically expressed in watts per square metre, arrives from all directions of the sky rather than from the solar disc. It contributes to the energy received by photovoltaic panels, especially under cloudy conditions.

definition: The shortwave solar radiation received directly from the sun's disc on a surface perpendicular to the sun's rays.
comment: It is usually expressed in watts per square metre. It is the key resource indicator for concentrating solar power and tracking PV systems.

definition: The radiant energy flux of solar radiation in the shortwave part of the spectrum passing through a unit area.
comment: Downward shortwave flux at the surface is the physical basis of the solar resource, and its value at the top of the atmosphere and surface is used to characterise atmospheric transmittance. It is usually expressed in watts per square metre.

definition: Power that could be generated by small hydropower development at a site or river reach.
comment: It is usually expressed in kilowatts or megawatts and is computed from discharge and head. It is used to identify and rank sites for small hydropower schemes.

definition: Electrical power that could theoretically be generated at a small hydropower site from its available flow and head.
comment: Small hydropower potential, typically expressed in kilowatts, is commonly computed from discharge, head, water density and gravitational acceleration. It is used to screen and rank candidate sites for small hydropower development.

definition: The steepness of the terrain surface, expressed as the rate of change of elevation with horizontal distance.
comment: Slope is given in degrees or percent and is derived from digital elevation models. It constrains the siting of solar, wind and hydropower installations and influences construction costs.

definition: The assessed degree to which a location is appropriate for siting a small hydropower dam.
comment: It is typically obtained by combining several physical, environmental and socio-economic criteria in a multi-criteria or GIS-based analysis to rank candidate sites.

definition: Amount of hydropower that could be developed through small-scale hydropower plants in a given area.
comment: It is usually expressed in kilowatts or megawatts. It supports planning of decentralised and rural electrification projects.

definition: Depth of liquid water that would result from melting the snowpack covering a unit area.
comment: Snow water equivalent, typically expressed in millimetres, quantifies water stored as snow. It is important for forecasting snowmelt-driven streamflow and reservoir inflow in mountainous basins.

definition: The amount of water held in the soil.
comment: It may be expressed as volumetric content or as an equivalent water depth. It influences runoff generation and evapotranspiration and is therefore important in hydrological modelling for hydropower.

definition: Ratio of the useful exergy delivered by a solar energy conversion system to the exergy of the incident solar radiation.
comment: Exergy efficiency accounts for the quality of energy as well as its quantity, unlike energy efficiency. It is used to evaluate and compare the thermodynamic performance of solar thermal and photovoltaic systems.

definition: The instantaneous power of solar radiation received per unit area of a surface.
comment: Usually expressed in watts per square metre, it differs from irradiation, which is energy accumulated over time. It is the direct driver of PV and solar thermal power output.

definition: The electrical energy or power produced by photovoltaic systems.
comment: It is the main output of photovoltaic plants and is used to assess system performance, contribution to supply and economic viability. It is expressed in power or energy units such as kilowatts or kilowatt-hours.

definition: Electrical power produced by a solar photovoltaic system.
comment: It is usually expressed in watts or kilowatts. It depends on irradiance, temperature and system characteristics and is the typical target of PV performance analysis and forecasting.

definition: Electromagnetic energy emitted by the sun and received at a surface or in the atmosphere.
comment: Solar radiation, expressed as an instantaneous irradiance or as an irradiation total such as megajoules per square metre per day, is the basic resource for solar energy. It is also an input to hydrological and crop models through its role in evapotranspiration.

definition: The maximum useful work that can be obtained from incident solar radiation.
comment: Exergy accounts for the quality of radiant energy and is lower than the total radiant energy. It is used to evaluate the thermodynamic potential and conversion efficiency of solar energy systems.

definition: The thermal power produced by collecting and converting solar radiation into heat.
comment: In concentrating solar power plants, the thermal power from the solar field feeds a power block or thermal storage and determines electricity output. It is usually expressed in megawatts thermal.

definition: Number density of particles in the solar wind, the stream of charged plasma emitted by the Sun.
comment: It is usually expressed in particles per cubic centimetre. It is a space-weather quantity unrelated to terrestrial wind energy and is mainly used in heliospheric and geomagnetic modelling.

definition: The angle between the local vertical and the direction of the sun.
comment: It controls the path length of sunlight through the atmosphere and the intensity of radiation on horizontal surfaces, and is used in solar geometry, radiation modelling and forecasting. It is usually expressed in degrees.

definition: Hydropower potential of a river normalised by the length of the reach considered.
comment: It is usually expressed in kilowatts per kilometre. It allows comparison of the hydropower richness of river reaches of different lengths.

definition: Second power of the wind speed.
comment: The square of wind speed is proportional to the kinetic energy per unit mass of moving air. It appears in derivations of wind energy and in statistical moments of wind-speed distributions.

definition: The standard deviation of wind speed values over a given averaging period.
comment: It quantifies wind speed variability and, divided by the mean wind speed, gives turbulence intensity. It is used in turbine loading assessment and site classification.

definition: Volume of water flowing through a stream cross-section per unit time.
comment: Stream discharge, typically expressed in cubic metres per second, is the standard measure of river flow. It is used to calibrate hydrological models and to estimate hydropower potential.

definition: A hierarchical ranking of a stream segment within a river network based on the number and order of its tributaries.
comment: The Strahler system is the most common scheme. Higher-order streams generally carry larger flows, so stream order is used to screen river reaches for hydropower potential.

definition: Flow of water in a natural channel such as a stream or river, quantified as volume per unit time.
comment: Streamflow, typically expressed in cubic metres per second, integrates precipitation, evapotranspiration and storage in a catchment. It is the main resource variable for hydropower and a common target of hydrological modelling.

definition: The part of streamflow that reaches the channel through subsurface pathways rather than overland flow.
comment: It includes interflow and baseflow contributions and sustains river flow during dry periods. It is a component of the water balance in hydrological models.

definition: The angular elevation of the sun above the horizon.
comment: It is the complement of the solar zenith angle and determines the incidence of solar radiation, shading and daily irradiance profiles for solar energy systems. It is usually expressed in degrees.

definition: Length of time during which direct solar radiation exceeds a defined threshold at a location.
comment: It is usually expressed in hours per day. It is widely measured and is used in empirical models to estimate global solar radiation where radiation data are lacking.

definition: Temperature of the air near the ground, conventionally measured at about 2 m above the surface.
comment: Surface air temperature, typically expressed in degrees Celsius, is a standard meteorological observation. It is used to estimate solar radiation, air density and photovoltaic module temperature.

definition: The rate of energy transfer from the surface to the atmosphere associated with evaporation and transpiration of water.
comment: Usually expressed in watts per square metre, it is a major component of the surface energy balance. It influences atmospheric stability and boundary-layer development.

definition: The atmospheric pressure at the Earth's surface at a given location.
comment: It is used with temperature to compute air density for wind power estimation and is a standard variable in reanalysis and weather model outputs. It is usually expressed in pascals or hectopascals.

definition: Measure of the irregularity of the land or water surface that resists airflow near the ground.
comment: It is often characterised by the roughness length in metres. It controls the shape of the vertical wind profile and thus the extrapolation of wind speed to turbine hub height.

definition: Exponent of the power-law relationship describing how wind speed changes with height above the ground.
comment: Also called the wind shear exponent, it is dimensionless and depends on surface roughness and atmospheric stability. It is used to extrapolate measured wind speeds to turbine hub height.

definition: The height above the surface at which the extrapolated logarithmic wind profile reaches zero wind speed.
comment: The aerodynamic roughness length characterises how strongly surface features slow the wind. It is essential for extrapolating wind speeds to turbine hub height.

definition: The portion of runoff that flows over the land surface into streams without infiltrating into the soil.
comment: It is the fast-responding component of river discharge and influences flood peaks, sediment transport and the timing of inflows to hydropower reservoirs. It is usually expressed as a depth of water such as millimetres per year.

definition: The elevation of the water surface in the tailrace channel downstream of a hydropower turbine.
comment: Usually expressed in metres, the tailrace level is subtracted from the headwater level to obtain gross head. Higher tailrace levels reduce the available head and power output.

definition: The portion of theoretical hydropower potential that can be exploited with current technology, accounting for efficiencies and technical constraints.
comment: It is a key intermediate in hydropower resource assessment, lying between theoretical and economically feasible potential. It is usually expressed in kilowatts or in energy per year.

definition: Physical quantity expressing the degree of hotness or coldness of a substance or medium.
comment: Temperature, typically expressed in degrees Celsius or kelvin, is a fundamental thermodynamic variable. In renewable-energy assessment it affects air density, photovoltaic efficiency and many empirical resource models.

definition: The difference between two air temperature values, such as the daily maximum and minimum temperatures.
comment: The daily temperature range is related to cloudiness and atmospheric transmittance and is used in empirical models to estimate solar radiation. It is usually expressed in degrees Celsius.

definition: Steepness of the land surface, expressed as the rate of change of elevation with horizontal distance.
comment: It is usually expressed in degrees or percent and derived from a digital elevation model. Slope constrains the siting of solar and wind installations and influences runoff and hydropower layout.

definition: Total water stored on and below the land surface, including surface water, soil moisture, groundwater, snow and ice.
comment: Terrestrial water storage, typically expressed as an equivalent water depth in millimetres, is observable from satellite gravimetry. It is used to assess regional water availability and constrain hydrological models.

definition: The maximum hydropower that could be generated from water flow and elevation drop, assuming complete conversion without losses.
comment: It is computed from discharge and head and represents an upper bound on exploitable energy. Technical and economic potentials are derived from it by accounting for constraints.

definition: Degree to which a location is exposed to or sheltered from the wind by surrounding terrain in a given direction.
comment: Topographic exposure is derived from terrain elevation relative to the surroundings. It is used to account for terrain effects on local wind speed and in wind resource and wind-damage studies.

definition: The shape and elevation configuration of the land surface.
comment: Topography governs head availability and drainage for hydropower, wind flow acceleration and sheltering for wind energy, and shading for solar energy, making it a key siting factor.

definition: Electrical power delivered by a turbine at a given moment or under given conditions.
comment: Turbine power output, typically expressed in kilowatts or megawatts, is determined by the turbine power curve and the available resource. It is the basis for estimating energy production of wind or hydropower installations.

definition: The volume of water passed through hydropower turbines over a given period.
comment: It is the portion of reservoir outflow used for power generation. Together with head, it determines the energy produced by the plant.

definition: The ratio of the standard deviation of wind speed to the mean wind speed over a given averaging period.
comment: It characterises short-term wind fluctuations that affect turbine fatigue loads, power curve performance and turbine class selection. It is dimensionless and often expressed as a percentage.

definition: Mean kinetic energy per unit mass associated with turbulent fluctuations of air velocity.
comment: It is usually expressed in square metres per square second. It characterises turbulence intensity in the boundary layer, which affects turbine loads, wake recovery and wind profile modelling.

definition: The portion of power from an energy source that can actually be delivered for use after conversion losses and operational limits.
comment: For wind turbines it is lower than the power available in the wind because of aerodynamic, mechanical and electrical limits. It is usually expressed in kilowatts.

definition: Rate of change of air temperature with height in the atmosphere.
comment: It is expressed as a temperature difference per unit height or between two levels. It indicates atmospheric stability, which influences vertical mixing and the shape of the wind profile.

definition: The volume of water passing a given point per unit time.
comment: It is expressed in units such as cubic metres per second or per day. It is central to both hydropower assessments and water pumping applications.

definition: A modelled quantity representing the lower tail of a five-parameter Wakeby probability distribution.
comment: The Wakeby distribution is a flexible model used in frequency analysis of hydrological and climatic extremes, and its lower tail characterises low-value events such as low flows.

definition: Parameter of the Wakeby probability distribution that sets the lower bound or position of the distribution along the variable axis.
comment: It has the same units as the modelled variable. It is estimated, often by L-moments, when fitting the flexible five-parameter Wakeby distribution to wind-speed or hydrological data.

definition: Target quantile values at selected non-exceedance probabilities used to fit the upper tail of a Wakeby distribution.
comment: The Wakeby distribution is a flexible five-parameter distribution often fitted with L-moments. Specifying upper-tail targets helps represent extreme values such as high flows or wind speeds.

definition: The volume of water passing through a channel cross-section per unit time.
comment: Discharge is the primary hydrological input to hydropower potential calculations and flow-duration analysis. It is usually expressed in cubic metres per second.

definition: Height of a water surface above a reference datum at a given location.
comment: It is usually expressed in metres. River and reservoir levels are linked to discharge and storage and are routinely monitored for hydropower operation and flood management.

definition: Volume of water delivered by a pumping system over a given period.
comment: Water produced, typically expressed in cubic metres, is the main performance output of water-pumping systems. It is used to evaluate and size renewable-powered pumping systems against water requirements.

definition: The quantity of water lifted by a pumping system over a given period.
comment: It is usually expressed as a volume. In wind and solar water pumping, it is the main measure of useful system output.

definition: The mass of water vapour per unit mass of dry air.
comment: It is a conserved measure of atmospheric moisture used in weather and climate models and influences air density, cloud formation and solar radiation transmission. It is usually expressed in kilograms per kilogram or grams per kilogram.

definition: Speed of water flow at a point or averaged over a channel cross-section.
comment: It is usually expressed in metres per second. It is used to compute discharge and to assess hydrokinetic and run-of-river energy potential.

definition: Amount of water leaving a catchment as surface and subsurface flow over a given period, often expressed as an equivalent depth.
comment: Water yield, typically expressed in millimetres or as a volume, reflects precipitation minus evapotranspiration and storage change. It indicates the water available for hydropower and other uses and is used in hydrological model calibration.

definition: The ratio of the length of a hydropower waterway to the gross head it provides.
comment: This dimensionless ratio indicates how much conduit length is needed per unit of head. Lower values generally mean lower construction cost and losses, making it useful for ranking small hydropower sites.

definition: The reduction of wind power output below what could be generated given the available wind resource.
comment: Curtailment arises from grid constraints, oversupply or system balancing needs and represents lost renewable energy, motivating storage, demand flexibility and grid reinforcement. It is expressed in megawatts or megawatt-hours.

definition: Direction from which the wind blows.
comment: It is usually expressed in degrees clockwise from north or as compass sectors. It is used to build wind roses and to optimise turbine layout and orientation.

definition: Kinetic energy contained in moving air that can be converted into useful energy.
comment: Wind energy available at a site depends on air density and the distribution of wind speeds over time. Estimating it, typically in kilowatt-hours, is a core step in wind resource assessment.

definition: The wind energy available per unit area swept perpendicular to the wind over a given period.
comment: It is derived from air density and the distribution of wind speeds. It is used to compare wind resources between sites independently of turbine choice.

definition: The electrical energy generated by wind turbines or wind farms over a period.
comment: It is the main performance indicator of wind power projects, used for yield assessment, economic evaluation and grid integration studies. It is usually expressed in megawatt-hours or gigawatt-hours.

definition: Total rated power of all turbines in a wind farm.
comment: It is usually expressed in megawatts. It sets the maximum output of the wind farm and, with the capacity factor, its expected energy production.

definition: Total electrical power delivered by all turbines of a wind farm.
comment: Wind-farm output power, typically expressed in megawatts, accounts for the wind resource, turbine characteristics and losses such as wake effects. It is used to estimate farm energy production and grid impact.
