definition: The energy contained in the wind that is theoretically available for extraction.
comment: It is derived from air density and wind speed and represents the resource before turbine conversion limits. It is used to compare the energy implied by fitted wind speed distributions with observations.

definition: The kinetic power of the wind per unit area perpendicular to the flow.
comment: It is proportional to air density and the cube of wind speed and is a standard indicator for classifying wind resource quality. It is usually expressed in watts per square metre.

definition: Probability distribution describing how wind power density is distributed across its possible values at a site.
comment: It is derived from the wind-speed probability distribution and air density. It shows which wind-speed ranges contribute most to the available energy and supports turbine selection.

definition: Electrical energy or power produced by wind turbines.
comment: Wind power generation depends on the wind resource at hub height and on turbine performance. It is a central output in wind energy assessments and in the planning of power systems with high renewable shares.

definition: The magnitude of the horizontal velocity of moving air.
comment: Wind speed, usually in metres per second, is the primary variable in wind resource assessment. Because power in the wind scales with the cube of wind speed, small errors strongly affect energy estimates.

variableName: wind speed at the 850 hpa pressure level
definition: Wind speed at the 850 hPa pressure level of the atmosphere.
comment: The 850 hPa level typically lies around 1.5 km above sea level, above most surface friction effects. Its wind speed is used as a large-scale predictor in downscaling and reanalysis-based studies.

definition: The wind speed at which the wind energy density distribution of a site reaches its maximum.
comment: Derived from the wind speed distribution, it indicates the wind speed contributing most to the annual energy and is used to match turbine rated speed to the site. It is usually expressed in metres per second.

definition: Wind speed measured or estimated close to the ground, typically at a standard height of about 10 m.
comment: It is usually expressed in metres per second. Near-surface values are widely available from stations and are extrapolated vertically to estimate wind at turbine hub heights.

definition: Function describing the relative likelihood of each wind-speed value at a site.
comment: The wind-speed probability density is usually represented by a fitted distribution such as Weibull or Rayleigh. It is combined with turbine power curves to estimate mean power and energy production.

definition: The probability distribution describing how frequently different wind speeds occur at a location.
comment: It is commonly modelled with Weibull or Rayleigh distributions. Combined with a turbine power curve, it is used to estimate expected energy production.

definition: The total electrical energy generated by a wind turbine over one year.
comment: It is the key yield metric for comparing turbines and sites and for computing capacity factor and levelized cost of energy. It is usually expressed in megawatt-hours per year.

definition: Ratio of the actual energy produced by a wind turbine over a period to the energy it would produce operating at rated power for the whole period.
comment: It is usually expressed as a percentage. It summarises how well a turbine matches the local wind resource and is a key indicator of project performance and economics.

definition: Electrical energy produced by a wind turbine over a given period.
comment: Wind turbine energy output, typically expressed in kilowatt-hours or megawatt-hours, is obtained from the turbine power curve and the wind-speed distribution. It is used to evaluate turbine performance and project viability.

definition: The electrical power produced by a wind turbine.
comment: It depends on wind speed through the turbine power curve and is usually expressed in kilowatts or megawatts. It is the basic output quantity of wind energy systems.

definition: The electrical power produced by a wind turbine.
comment: It depends on wind speed according to the turbine power curve and is used to estimate energy yield and assess turbine performance. It is usually expressed in kilowatts or megawatts.

definition: Ratio of the standard deviation of wind speed to the mean wind speed over a given averaging interval.
comment: It is dimensionless and is often called turbulence intensity. High values increase fatigue loads on turbines and reduce power-curve performance, so it is used in site suitability and turbine class selection.

definition: Speed and direction of the motion of air relative to the Earth surface.
comment: Wind velocity is a vector quantity whose magnitude is the wind speed, typically expressed in metres per second. It is the fundamental variable for wind resource assessment and wind power estimation.

definition: The east-west component of the horizontal wind vector.
comment: It is positive for wind blowing towards the east and is usually expressed in metres per second. Combined with the meridional component, it gives wind speed and direction in reanalysis and model data.

definition: The west-to-east component of the horizontal wind vector.
comment: Together with the meridional component it fully describes horizontal wind and is the form in which wind is provided by most reanalysis and weather models. It is usually expressed in metres per second.

definition: Component of the horizontal wind velocity directed along the east-west axis.
comment: It is usually expressed in metres per second, positive towards the east. Combined with the meridional component it gives wind speed and direction, and it is a standard output of reanalysis and weather models.
